name: Fogo Island
reservation: There is no entry fee for the island itself, but ferry space from Farewell is limited and operates on a first-come, first-served basis without reservations for standard vehicles. Accommodation on the island is very limited and often booked months in advance; always confirm lodging before boarding the ferry. Check the provincial ferry service website for current schedules and potential weather delays.

days.title: Fishing Heritage and Longshots

stops.name: Brimstone Head
stops.detail: Hike the wooden boardwalks to what is locally touted as one of the four corners of the flat earth for panoramic views of the Atlantic.

stops.name: Tilting National Historic Site
stops.detail: Walk through this Irish-settled fishing village to see the traditional wooden flakes and stages used for drying cod.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for island road navigation between communities; conditions vary.
days.note: Fog can roll in rapidly, significantly reducing visibility on the coastal trails.

days.title: Modern Art and Ancient Rocks
days.start: Suggested: 8:30 AM from Joe Batt's Arm

stops.name: Long Studio
stops.detail: View the striking contemporary architecture of this off-grid artist studio, contrasting with the rugged 400-million-year-old shoreline.

stops.name: The Great Auk Statue
stops.detail: Visit the sculpture dedicated to the extinct flightless bird that once nested on nearby Funk Island.

days.driving: Allow 1.5 hours for local stops and coastal walking; conditions vary.
days.note: Most artist studios are private workspaces; view from the exterior unless an open house is scheduled.

days.title: Island Heights and Harbour Life

stops.name: Lion's Den Trail
stops.detail: Trek the loop connecting four former 'outport' communities that were resettled, offering views of the rugged cliffs.

stops.name: Fogo Island Marine Interpretive Centre
stops.detail: Learn about the island's transition from the cod fishery to its current cultural economy.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for driving and significant time for hiking; conditions vary.
days.note: Moose are frequently spotted near the roadsides at dusk; exercise caution while driving.

intel.title: Ferry Terminal Queuing
intel.text: Vehicle lineups at Farewell can exceed several hours during peak summer weekends. Arrive significantly early and be prepared for the possibility of waiting for a second or third sailing.

intel.title: Outport Connectivity
intel.text: Signal is generally available in the main towns like Fogo and Joe Batt's Arm but drops off entirely on the central barrens. Download maps before leaving the mainland.

intel.title: Limited Island Pumps
intel.text: There are very few fuel stations on the island, primarily in the town of Fogo. Ensure you have a full tank before leaving the mainland at Gander or Farewell.

intel.title: Iceberg and Berry Seasons
intel.text: Icebergs are typically visible from the shore in June, while berry picking season begins in August. Shops and museums may have reduced hours outside of the peak July window.

intel.title: Ferry Dependency
intel.text: Island access is entirely dependent on the MV Veteran ferry; mechanical issues or high winds can cancel service for days. Always have a contingency plan for a delayed return to the mainland.

plan.arrival: Fly into Gander, rent a vehicle, and drive north to Farewell. Check the ferry status board at the Gander airport or online before starting the drive.
plan.vehicle: A standard passenger car is sufficient for the paved island roads, though an SUV offers more comfort on gravel turn-offs; check ferry rates for oversized RVs.
plan.goldenHour: Brimstone Head at sunset, offering elevated views of the sun dipping into the Labrador Sea during clear summer nights.
